title: Mother Pearl
text: Gyða’s third solo album of original compositions, out on Marvaða. On vinyl and digital.
story:

With Úlfur Hansson, Bert Cools, Indrė Jurgelevičiūtė, Alex Sopp, Julian Sartorius and Katie Buckley, and Kjartan Sveinsson co-writing the title track.

title: Ox
text: Both visceral & wildly sublime, Ox celebrates the embodiment of both the darkness and the light that exists within us.
story:
By turns both visceral and wildly sublime, Ox celebrates the embodiment of both the darkness and the light that exist within us. The title comes from the opening song, ‘Alphabet’, as most alphabets begin with the letter aleph, originating from the Egyptian hieroglyph which depicts an ox’s head.

On Ox, Gyða presents the vast versatility of her work, demonstrating the ways in which song-making is a form of alchemy: a transformative process of taking something from the darkness and bringing it into light. The result is an album of otherworldly spaciousness and urgent, fearless intimacy all at once.

title: Epicycle
text: A constellation of composition, from ancient to avant-garde.
story:
“With Epicycle I want to bring out that silver thread of mutual resonance that runs beyond time or space. I hope this record quietly will dissolve walls by simply not sensing their existence.

I’m an architectural seamstress of a space, a new equation made simply by following the geometry of sensation. I pull out the silver threads of recognition that I find in those creations left behind, I draw the lines between those eight stars and weave a diamond net, a new constellation in our multi-cosmic galaxy. Each star engenders a new angle out of one another, calls out quiet overtones and runs smoothly as one, and thus as a whole creates a ripple effect in the tapestry of space and time.”

— Gyða
quotes:
It’s evocative, moving, and reminds you that the power of music transcends time and space.
— Reykjavík Grapevine
